title: Pulse: live observability and incident console
tagline: A Datadog-style console with a hand-built Canvas chart engine and query language, running on a simulated backend in a Web Worker.
summary: I built a browser-only observability console: live-streaming metrics, a 240k-line log explorer with its own query language, alert rules, and a full incident workflow. Everything runs on a seeded simulator in a Web Worker, and a guided mission lets visitors investigate a planted outage end to end. I wrote the chart renderer and the query engine from scratch, with no charting or UI libraries.
highlights: I hand-built a Canvas 2D time-series renderer: min/max pixel-bucket decimation that provably preserves spikes, a two-layer canvas, DPR-correct sizing, off-screen skipping and a single rAF loop that only runs when something is dirty.

I implemented linked interaction across charts: brush-to-zoom, shift-drag pan, cursor-anchored wheel zoom, keyboard time navigation, a crosshair and tooltip synchronised across every chart, deploy markers and threshold lines.

I wrote a log query language from scratch (tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, compiler to typed-column predicates) with positioned syntax and semantic errors, syntax highlighting, autocomplete, saved queries and filter chips, and a hand-windowed list over 240k rows.

I put the simulation in a Web Worker behind a typed message protocol: seeded generators for 64 metric series and 240k logs, injected incidents (bad deploy, error burst, memory leak), live alert evaluation, and rollbacks that make the metrics actually recover.
I built the incident workflow: declare from an alert, auto-attached timeline of alerts, deploys and notes, status steps, runbook, rollback, and a post-mortem summary generated from measured data.

I built a self-checking guided mission whose steps are detected from real application state, and verified it with 30 unit tests plus a 35-check real-Chrome end-to-end script driven by mouse and keyboard.
